questions: When reversing the string because it contains no letters, should the reversal be applied to the original string or to the string after any potential case-swapping operations (which would be none in this case, but the order matters conceptually)?
What constitutes a 'letter'? Is it limited to ASCII A-Z/a-z, or does it include Unicode letters like 'é' or 'α'?
If the string contains at least one letter, but also non-letters, should the non-letters be left unchanged in position, or is the entire string reversed in that case?
For the case-swapping, is it applied to every character individually, or is there any interaction between characters (like swapping case based on neighboring characters)?
Should the function handle None input or non-string types, and if so, what should be returned?
When reversing the string due to no letters, does 'reverse the string' mean reversing the sequence of characters exactly, including any special characters or spaces, as in standard string reversal?

If the string contains letters, but after swapping case, some letters become non-letters (e.g., due to Unicode case mapping quirks), could that affect the 'contains no letters' condition retroactively?
Is the reversal performed in-place on the modified string (after case changes) or on the original string? This matters only if there are no letters, but the spec could be misinterpreted.
